findings.title: Broken Radar Visualization
findings.problem: The radar is a dark, empty disc with no active scanning animation or visible contact points. It reads as a broken component rather than a live instrument.
findings.why: Instantly undermines immersion and breaks the 'survival' atmosphere before gameplay begins. Fails to convey that the car is active or scanning for threats.
findings.fix: Add a rotating, animated cyan sweep line and inject 1-2 faint white 'blips' on the screen edge to simulate active scanning of distant enemies.

findings.title: Invisible Targeting Indicator
findings.problem: The player's orange vehicle is surrounded by an active selection box, but there is no visible cursor, crosshair, or arrow indicating which specific object is targeted or highlighted.
findings.why: Creates confusion during fast-paced movement. Players cannot distinguish between UI-selected objects and in-game interactive entities like gates or buildings, reducing playability.
findings.fix: Overlay a thin, high-contrast yellow arrow or crosshair directly above the selected vehicle to clearly indicate the active target or destination.

findings.title: Destructive UI Occlusion
findings.problem: The central vehicle is perfectly aligned with the middle lane marker, causing the vehicle to obscure the lane line completely, while the surrounding environment is heavily pixelated.
findings.why: Blurs the visual center of attention. At speed, players rely on peripheral lane markers to judge alignment, but here the marker is hidden by the vehicle itself, making navigation feel imprecise and sloppy.
findings.fix: Add a subtle downward-pointing highlight or glow effect around the vehicle's base to visually separate it from the road surface, ensuring the lane markings remain clearly readable.

findings.title: Flat, Indistinguishable Map
findings.problem: The map consists of flat grey tiles and simple geometric blocks with no depth, terrain variation, or environmental context. All buildings and obstacles look identical in color and texture.
findings.why: Makes navigation difficult and the world feel lifeless. Lack of visual hierarchy prevents players from distinguishing between critical structures (e.g., gates vs. buildings) and reduces strategic clarity.
findings.fix: Introduce color-coded outlines or background shading on buildings to differentiate key points (e.g., gates in bright red, buildings in muted blue) and add slight perspective shading to create a sense of depth.

findings.title: Low-Contrast Text Hierarchy
findings.where: Vehicle Constructor Screen (left and right panels)
findings.problem: Key stats and options are rendered in low-contrast white/grey text on dark backgrounds, making it hard to distinguish between critical actions (e.g., 'Build this vehicle') and secondary information.
findings.why: Obscures the most important decision points. Players may struggle to prioritize key actions like naming the vehicle or selecting weapons, leading to confusion and wasted time.
